name: Thunderbird
tagline: A desktop mail client with calendar and contacts
description: Mail, calendars, contacts and feeds in one desktop application, plus an Android app. It works with any standards-based mailbox and can also connect to Exchange, which makes it a useful first step before changing where your mail lives.
backing: MZLA Technologies, a subsidiary of the Mozilla Foundation, funded almost entirely by user donations

maturity.rationale: More than twenty years old, with a donation-funded full-time team, monthly releases and a modernised interface.

strengths: Works with any IMAP or POP mailbox, and with CalDAV and CardDAV for calendars and contacts
Connects to Exchange mailboxes, so you can change client first and server later
The same application on Windows, macOS and Linux, with a unified inbox across accounts
weaknesses: It is only a client: you still need a mailbox somewhere
Exchange support covers mail first; calendar and address-book sync with Exchange Online has been arriving in stages, so check the current release notes
Outlook .pst archives must be converted, or imported on a Windows machine that still has Outlook, before Thunderbird can read them

featureNotes.spam-filtering: Trainable junk filter in the client
featureNotes.exchange-protocols: Native Exchange mail; calendar and contacts still rolling out
featureNotes.free-busy: Shows colleagues' availability when the calendar server provides it
